acceptance_criteria.criterion: renderChunksToMarkdown() produces Markdown output structurally consistent with the orchestrator's serialize_messages_to_markdown() format.
The renderer correctly merges token-level chunk data into complete messages before rendering.
Subagent messages (identified by namespace) are grouped and labelled appropriately.
The function handles empty input (returns minimal valid Markdown) and malformed JSONL lines (skips them gracefully).

summary: Created mcp-server/gui/chunk-renderer.ts — pure TypeScript module implementing renderChunksToMarkdown(jsonlContent: string): string.
Implemented JSONL parsing with chunk_format:1 header validation; both object-shape {ns, msg, metadata} and array-shape [ns, msg, metadata] chunk lines are supported.

Merges token-level AIMessageChunk data (content string concatenation, list-of-blocks merging by index, tool_call_chunks accumulation by index, usage_metadata summation) into complete messages keyed by message id.
Groups messages by namespace: empty namespace = main agent (rendered first, no extra heading), non-empty namespace = sub-agent (rendered under '### Subagent: {key}' heading).

Renders Markdown structurally consistent with dialogue_writer.py's serialize_messages_to_markdown(): h1 document heading + metadata table, ## Role sections, fenced tool-call blocks, horizontal-rule + ## Token Usage footer.
Handles empty input (returns minimal valid Markdown with '*No messages recorded.*') and malformed JSONL lines (silently skipped — no throw).

Wrote 35 unit tests in tests/gui/chunk-renderer.test.ts covering all acceptance criteria: empty input variants, single message, multi-turn, token merging, tool-call merging, mixed content blocks, subagent grouping, malformed lines, structural consistency, array-shape lines, missing header.
All 1795 existing tests continue to pass; 35 new tests all pass.

comments.note: chunk-renderer.ts uses a hand-rolled merge for list-of-blocks content (mergeContent). If LangChain ever surfaces a richer block schema (e.g., multiple block types with IDs rather than positional indexes), this will need updating. A comment in the code already flags the positional-index assumption; no action needed now.

The rendered Markdown heading is hard-coded to '# Dialogue — streaming capture'. WP-006 will wire this into a rendered endpoint; if the consuming UI needs stage/wp_id metadata in the heading, the function signature could be extended to accept optional metadata params. Deferred to WP-006 scope.

The JSONL chunk format supports two wire shapes (object {ns,msg,metadata} and array [ns,msg,metadata]). WP-002's notes reference the object shape, but both are handled defensively. Worth confirming the final Python implementation uses only one shape and documenting it in the WP-002 notes to avoid future confusion.

summary: Build check: chunk-renderer.ts compiles cleanly (TypeScript, no errors) and is importable as an ES module via the project's vitest runner.

AC1 — Structural consistency with serialize_messages_to_markdown(): PASS. Output includes # h1 heading, metadata table, ## Role sections, fenced tool-call blocks, and --- + ## Token Usage footer. Verified by structural-consistency test suite (5 tests).

AC2 — Token-level chunk merging: PASS. String concatenation of same-id chunks verified (500-chunk stress test + 3 unit tests). List-of-blocks merging by positional index verified. usage_metadata summation across chunks and messages verified.

AC3 — Subagent grouping: PASS. Non-empty namespace arrays produce '### Subagent: {key}' headings; main agent (empty ns) is always rendered first; multiple distinct namespaces each get their own heading; same-namespace messages are grouped under a single heading. Stress-tested with 10 concurrent namespaces.

AC4 — Empty input and malformed JSONL handling: PASS. Empty string, whitespace-only, and header-only inputs all return minimal valid Markdown with '*No messages recorded.*'. Invalid JSON, scalars, missing-ns objects, and mixed good/bad lines are all skipped gracefully without throwing.
AC5 — All unit tests pass: PASS. All 35 Developer-authored unit tests pass. Full suite of 1795 tests passes with 0 regressions.

Edge-case stress tests (QA-authored, 6 scenarios): all PASS — 500-chunk single-message merge, Unicode/emoji content, null content field, 10 simultaneous subagent namespaces, unparseable tool-call args fallback, missing 'ns' field skip.

metrics.test_coverage: 35 unit tests + 6 QA edge-case stress tests; all AC scenarios explicitly covered

comments.note: Edge case confirmed: a chunk with `content: null` does not throw — it silently produces an empty content slot. Behaviour is correct (the merged message renders as an empty section), but this case is not explicitly covered in the Developer's test suite. Consider adding a test for `content: null` in chunk-renderer.test.ts to pin the contract.
500-chunk merge stress test: performance is acceptable (~17ms for 500 chunks). No O(n²) behaviour observed. The positional-index merge loop in mergeContent() is linear per chunk, as expected.

Unparseable tool-call args (e.g. truncated JSON mid-stream) fall back to rendering the raw arg string inside the ```json fence. This is a safe and readable degradation. No action needed, but worth documenting in the module's JSDoc as an explicit contract.

summary: Code review PASS. chunk-renderer.ts is a high-quality, well-architected pure TypeScript module. All four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context) are satisfactory. One trivial Fix-Forward applied (renderContent type annotation). comments.note: No blocking issues found. Architecture is clean: types → helpers → parsing → accumulation → rendering → public API. The single exported function provides a narrow, composable API that is easy to consume in WP-006 route wiring.

renderContent() signature on line 131 declared 'content: string | ContentBlock[] | undefined' but the null guard on line 132 ('if (content === undefined || content === null)') handled null at runtime without it being declared in the type. Updated signature to 'string | ContentBlock[] | null | undefined' to match actual behaviour. Non-behavioral change — no logic was modified.

The 'as Record<string, number>' cast on line 439 for usage_metadata is safe in practice because mergeUsageMetadata() guards each value with 'typeof value === "number"' before summing. However, the cast silences TypeScript's type narrowing. Low risk, acceptable for this WP scope.

[documentation-forward] The renderToolCalls() function silently falls back to rendering unparseable tool-call args as a raw string inside a ```json fence (line 171-172). This is a useful contract but is not documented in the module-level JSDoc or in the renderToolCalls() function comment. Add a JSDoc note to renderToolCalls() documenting the fallback behaviour explicitly so future consumers understand what the rendered output looks like when args are truncated mid-stream.

[documentation-forward] The JSONL format section of the module-level JSDoc (lines 12-21) documents the chunk format but does not explicitly state that both object-shape {ns,msg,metadata} AND array-shape [ns,msg,metadata] are supported. Update the JSDoc to mention both wire shapes and note that both are handled identically — this will save future contributors from having to read parseChunkLine() to discover this.

Token Usage footer key ordering is alphabetical (Object.keys().sort()) — this is stable and deterministic, which is the right choice for consistency. The QA handoff note flagged this as cosmetically non-semantic. No action required; alphabetical ordering is preferable to insertion order for a rendered table.

summary: Resolved both documentation-forward items raised by the Reviewer during code review.

Edit 1 — Module-level JSONL format JSDoc (lines 17-30): Expanded the 'Lines 1-N (chunks)' section to explicitly document both wire shapes — object shape {ns, msg, metadata} and array shape [namespace, msg_dump, metadata]. Added a clear note that both shapes are parsed identically and that parseChunkLine() normalises them to a common internal representation.
